title: Physics Won't Hurt You
subtitle: Well, kind of. A history of physics from falling apples to the edge of everything
based_on: the documented history of physics and physicists, plus an honest, clearly-flagged tour of the field's live open questions and speculative frontiers (interpretations of quantum mechanics, the simulation hypothesis, string/loop quantum gravity, consciousness-and-physics crossover, and the ethics of physics) — ORIGINAL SYNTHESIS in the author's own words, not a derivative of any single existing popular-science book
author: Andries J. Greyling
protagonist: an ensemble cast of physicists across four centuries, narrated by a warm, funny, plain-spoken authorial voice (Bryson/Sapiens register)
setting: Pisa to Cambridge to Princeton to Los Alamos to CERN to the edge of the observable universe, c. 1590-present
logline: Physics is the story of people who kept insisting the universe would answer plain questions if you asked it plainly enough — from a man dropping balls off a tower to a machine at CERN finding a particle that gives everything else mass — told with the same curiosity and dark humour it deserves, all the way out to the edge where physics runs out of answers and hands the questions to philosophy.
blueprint: five-part cradle-to-frontier survey: (I) The Old Certainties - classical mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics; (II) Everything Falls Apart - the quantum revolution; (III) Splitting the Atom, Drawing the Universe - the bomb, QED, the Standard Model; (IV) The Universe Gets Big - cosmology; (V) Where Physics Goes to Die - interpretations, simulation hypothesis, string/loop quantum gravity, consciousness and panpsychism, the ethics of physics, closing epilogue, and a final source-grounded coda on G's speculative 420 Code framework
market: readers of Bill Bryson's A Short History of Nearly Everything, Yuval Noah Harari's Sapiens, Carlo Rovelli, Brian Greene, and Sean Carroll
status: DRAFT COMPLETE (31 ch across 5 parts + backmatter, source-grounded G coda, ~58k, 2026-08-30)
tone: warm, funny, plain-spoken, unafraid of the strange; wonder-forward and sympathetically exploratory once the book reaches the speculative frontier, while still being honest and clearly-flagged about what is mainstream consensus, live open question, or frankly speculative
dedication: For everyone who ever asked a question a grown-up couldn't answer, and kept asking anyway.
clearances: All historical figures depicted are deceased and long-documented public figures of major historical record (Galileo, Newton, Faraday, Maxwell, Boltzmann, Planck, Einstein, Bohr, Schrodinger, Heisenberg, Dirac, Rutherford, Feynman, Gell-Mann, Hubble, Lemaitre, Hawking, et al.) -> depictable. This is an ORIGINAL narrative synthesis built from the well-documented public/scientific record; no sentence is copied from any existing popular-science book (Bryson, Rovelli, Greene, Carroll, Gleick, or any physicist's own writing) - dialogue and interior colour are reconstructed in the author's own words, kept true to the documented frame, exactly as this house's practice requires for every true-story/plainly-told title on this shelf.
sensitivity_read: required before publication for Chapter 31's treatment of living artist Gerhard van Niekerk and the author's personal relationship with him. The chapter keeps testimony separate from evidence and distinguishes G's claims, AJ's arithmetic reproduction, and external scientific validation.
